synonyms: Ziziphus bubalina Licht. ex Roem. & Schult.

en.text: Ziziphus mucronata, known as the buffalo thorn, is a species of tree in the family Rhamnaceae, native to southern Africa. It is deciduous and may grow up to 17 metres tall. It can survive in a variety of soil types, occurring in many habitats, mostly open woodlands, often on soils deposited by rivers, and grows frequently on termite mounds. Its Zulu name “umLahlankosi” alludes to its use as a grave marker for tribal chiefs, while the Afrikaans name “Blinkblaar-wag-'n-bietjie” alludes to the shiny light green leaves and the hooked thorns.

fr.text: Ziziphus mucronata, le Jujubier de l'hyène, est une espèce de plantes à fleurs de la famille des Rhamnacées. C'est une plante ligneuse.

id.text: Ziziphus mucronata atau yang dikenal sebagai garkad kerbau, adalah pohon dari famili Rhamnaceae yang asli Afrika Selatan. Pohon ini bersifat gugur dan dapat mencapai tinggi hingga 17 meter. Ia mampu tumbuh di berbagai jenis tanah dan ditemukan di beragam habitat, terutama hutan terbuka, sering di tanah yang terbentuk dari endapan sungai, serta kerap tumbuh di gundukan rayap. Namanya dalam bahasa Zulu, umLahlankosi, merujuk pada penggunaannya sebagai penanda makam kepala suku, sementara nama dalam bahasa Afrikaans, Blinkblaar-wag-'n-bietjie, menggambarkan daun muda yang hijau mengkilap dan duri yang melengkung.

en.heading: Uses
en.text:
It makes a good perimeter barrier as its thorns are profuse on young shoots and are difficult to untangle because one points forward while the other points backward. Certain tribes believe the tree is safe to use as a shelter against lightning, and it may be planted as a grave marker for a deceased chief.

■ Medical uses
A blend made from the roots is used as a painkiller and for dysentery while the bark and leaves are used for respiratory ailments and sepsis on the skin. A paste made from the roots and leaves will treat boils, sores and swelling. The above may be attributed to the peptide alkaloids and antifungals isolated from the bark and leaves. Branches are used for protection of cattle kraal and sometimes on the graves of dead tribal members. The wood is used for implements and fuel. The leaves bark and roots are used medicinally and magically for pain relief, respiratory complaints and skin infections, especially for chest and stomach disorders. The leaves if crushed may be used to stop bleeding. Steam baths from the bark are used to purify and improve the complexion. In East Africa, roots are used for treating snake bites.

■ Nutritional uses
The leaves are edible and can be cooked into spinach. The seeds can be roasted and ground as a substitute for coffee. The Ovambo people use it to distill ombike, a traditional liquor. The leaves and fruits are also a valuable source of forage for livestock.

id.heading: Kegunaan
id.text: Berbagai bagian pohon ini memiliki banyak kegunaan medis dan praktis. Akar, kulit kayu, dan daun digunakan secara tradisional untuk mengobati rasa sakit, disentri, gangguan pernapasan, infeksi kulit, bisul, luka, dan pembengkakan. Daun yang dihancurkan dapat menghentikan pendarahan, sedangkan mandi uap dari kulit kayu digunakan untuk memurnikan dan merawat kulit. Di Afrika Timur, akar juga dimanfaatkan untuk mengobati gigitan ular. Selain kegunaan medis, cabang pohon digunakan untuk melindungi kandang ternak atau sebagai tanda makam, dan kayunya dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan bakar atau untuk membuat peralatan. Aktivitas ini terkait dengan kandungan senyawa bioaktif seperti alkaloid peptida dan anti jamur yang terdapat di kulit kayu dan daun.
